submissions.findingTextShort: A 16-RCT meta-analysis found no cognitive benefit from B12/B-complex supplementation in people without overt B12 deficiency or advanced neurologic disease.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression of 16 randomized controlled trials involving 6,276 participants without advanced neurological disease or overt vitamin B12 deficiency found no evidence that vitamin B12 alone or B-vitamin combinations improved cognitive subdomains. The synthesis also did not support a robust general enhancement effect on depressive symptoms or idiopathic fatigue. These findings directly constrain use of B12 as a cognition/energy enhancer in nondeficient populations.
submissions.populationContext: Participants without overt B12 deficiency or advanced neurologic disease across randomized trials.
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B12 alone or in B-vitamin combinations; formulation and co-nutrients varied.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This null enhancement evidence does not negate treatment of true deficiency. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: B12 therapy can correct biochemical deficiency, while cognitive improvement is concentrated in people with pre-existing deficiency rather than B12-replete users.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A review of vitamin B12, cognitive impairment, and treatment evidence found that high-dose oral or parenteral B12 reliably corrected biochemical deficiency and that cognitive improvement was observed chiefly in patients with pre-existing B12 deficiency or elevated homocysteine. B12 therapy did not improve cognition in patients without pre-existing deficiency. Deficiency correction is therefore a different clinical proposition from nootropic enhancement.
submissions.populationContext: People with low B12/deficiency and comparison populations without established deficiency.
submissions.usageContext: Oral or parenteral vitamin B12 treatment; route/form depends on clinical context.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Association between low B12 and neurodegenerative disease is not itself proof of treatment efficacy outside deficiency. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A neurologic B12-deficiency synthesis supports deficiency-related benefit context but found long-term cognitive improvement inconsistent.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of neurological implications of vitamin B12 deficiency reported short-term neurological/cognitive improvement in some susceptible deficient populations after correction, while longer-term supplementation findings were inconsistent and many controlled trials did not show sustained cognitive improvement. This reinforces the need to distinguish deficiency treatment from durable enhancement claims.
submissions.populationContext: B12-deficient or susceptible populations across heterogeneous studies.
submissions.usageContext: Vitamin B12 correction/supplementation in deficiency-related neurologic contexts.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Heterogeneous populations and durations constrain broad conclusions. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 Cochrane review treats pediatric B12 supplementation as a deficiency/growth-development question, not a generic cognition-enhancement proposition.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 Cochrane review evaluated vitamin B12 supplementation for growth, development, and cognition in children in the context of deficiency risk and nutritional status. This pediatric evidence domain is population- and deficiency-specific and should not be combined with adult nootropic claims or used to imply that routine B12 supplementation enhances cognition in B12-replete individuals.
submissions.populationContext: Children at varying risk of vitamin B12 deficiency across supplementation trials.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Pediatric growth/development evidence must remain separate from adult enhancement or deficiency-treatment claims. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live Cobalamin profile states deficiency-treatment outcomes with zero receipts, a generic form-only dosage string, and no explicit form-owner boundary.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current NOINDEX Cobalamin profile states that B12 corrects deficiency and prevents deficiency-related anemia/neuropathy while exposing sourceCount zero and no claim map. Its dosage fields contain only `capsule or softgel`, which is a product form rather than a regimen. Generic cobalamin also coexists with separate form-specific owners such as methylcobalamin, so evidence and dosing must not be silently shared across forms without an explicit ontology rule.
submissions.usageContext: Repository evidence-receipt, dosage-template, and entity-form boundary finding.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This record does not propose a consumer dose or absorb the separate methylcobalamin workpack. Keep NOINDEX until governed reconciliation.
